subject: Proposal: 16→32 GPU capacity expansion — rate card & throughput guarantees
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aperture.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Mon, 25 Jan 2027 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal conversation + capacity expansion (16→32 GPUs)

Hi Lauren,

Hope you’re well — our Q2 roadmap has two new features that will push inference demand up significantly. We’re coming up on our Redwood renewal and are evaluating whether to double our Dedicated pool from 16 → 32 GPUs.

Can you share a renewal proposal that includes:
- revised reserved per-hour pricing for a 32 GPU committed pool (12-month term)
- any throughput guarantees or SLA language for sustained high-utilization (we need predictable latency and capacity for production)
- what burst/overflow options exist if we exceed committed throughput during launches

Procurement is cc’d — they’ll need a ballpark to start internal approvals. Happy to schedule a quick call if that’s easier.

Thanks,
Samantha Lee
Head of ML Platform, Aperture AI
Samantha Lee | Aperture AI

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aperture.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Tue, 26 Jan 2027 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity expansion (16→32 GPUs)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask. I ran initial numbers and have attached a draft rate card and a mutual action plan to get approvals moving. Key points in this preliminary proposal:

- Capacity: move from 16 → 32 dedicated GPUs (same type as current pool).
- Term: 12-month committed reserved pool.
- Pricing (reserved): $9.75 per GPU-hour (committed pool rate) — this reflects a volume discount versus your current 16-GPU rate.
- Burst/overflow: access to burst capacity at on-demand rates (subject to regional capacity) with automated fallback policies; we can carve a small burst buffer for launches with advance notice.
- Throughput guarantee: contractual baseline of 1,050,000 tokens/hour aggregate for the 32-GPU pool, with remediation credits if the 95th percentile sustained throughput falls below baseline more than twice in a billing month.
- SLA: 99.9% uptime on the serving tier for Dedicated pools; extended retention of infra logs for audit (30 days).

Attached: Redwood_ratecard_v3.pdf, DRAFT_MutualActionPlan-Aperture.docx

If that looks directionally right, procurement and I can iterate on the order form and scope. I’m happy to jump on a 20-min call to walk through the throughput SLA and the remediation language with your SREs.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123

From: dev_patel@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aperture.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, procurement@aperture.ai
Date: Thu, 28 Jan 2027 14:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity expansion (technical addendum)

Samantha — quick technical note from infra on what we’d commit to for the 32-GPU pool:

- Instance spec: NVIDIA H100-equivalent, same instance family you have today.
- Sustained baseline: we can guarantee an aggregate baseline of 1.05M tokens/hour as Lauren wrote; practically this maps to continuous batching profiles and a KV prefix cache retained per-customer.
- Latency target: 95th percentile generation latency under the workload profile outlined in the MAP (50 token prompt / 150 token generation) — we’ll include a verification run prior to cutover.
- Capacity headroom: we recommend keeping a 10% burst buffer (3 extra GPUs) that can be invoked in an emergency while we scale the committed pool. We can convert that buffer into permanent capacity at a prorated rate if you choose.

I attached a short checklist of test runs we propose before the renewal effective date so the throughput guarantee is measured against a reproducible test harness.

—Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aperture.ai>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aperture.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 29 Jan 2027 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity expansion (pricing follow-up)

Thanks Lauren and Dev — this is helpful. A couple of follow-ups from procurement and finance: 

- Pricing: $9.75/GPU-hour is closer to our target, but to secure internal approval we need $9.25/GPU-hour for a 12-month commit (we’re targeting a fixed unit cost for budgeting).
- Trial burst: can we get a one-time 30-day burst credit to cover the initial launch period (est. +12 GPUs for three weeks) so we don’t need to renegotiate if launch demand spikes?
- Acceptance & verification: procurement wants a firm verification timeline for the throughput guarantee so we can tie payment milestones to the cutover.

If you can confirm those items, procurement will prepare a PO. Otherwise we’ll need to present the current number to finance by next week.

Samantha

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@aperture.ai>, procurement@aperture.ai
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Feb 2027 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + capacity expansion (final terms)

Samantha — appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. We’ve reviewed internally and can accommodate the key items to close this before your finance deadline:

Final negotiated terms (summary):
- Capacity: 32 GPU committed reserved pool (H100-equivalent) for 12 months.
- Pricing: $9.50 per GPU-hour for the committed pool (final). This reflects a blended concession between our list and your target.
- Burst credit: one-time 30-day burst credit to cover +12 GPUs for up to three weeks during launch (applies to net new usage above committed baseline).
- Throughput verification: Redwood and Aperture will run the verification harness within 14 days of the effective date; the contractual throughput baseline is 1,050,000 tokens/hour aggregate as previously described. Payment milestones can be tied to successful verification in the MAP.
- SLA & remedies: 99.9% uptime; remediation credits apply if throughput baseline misses target more than twice in a 30-day billing period.

Next steps: I’ve uploaded the revised order form and updated MAP to the Drive link (order-form-RDW-AP-2027-04.pdf). If procurement confirms PO language, Aditya will send a final invoice and we’ll schedule the verification run with Dev.

If that’s approved, can procurement email a signed PO by EOD Friday so legal and finance can finish processing?

Thanks — excited to keep expanding with Aperture.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0123
